        .skip-to-content{position:absolute;left:-9999px;top:auto;width:1px;height:1px;overflow:hidden}
        .skip-to-content:focus{position:fixed;top:0;left:0;width:auto;height:auto;padding:10px 15px;background:#000;color:#fff;text-decoration:none;z-index:9999}
        /* nav#menu starts display:none so its raw ~5000px-tall list of items
           doesn't blow out the parent header layout before mmenu inits.
           mmenu adds .mm-menu / .mm-init classes when it runs (now lazy-init
           on first hamburger click — see ui.js). Using display:none rather
           than visibility:hidden is critical: visibility keeps layout space
           and would push the page down 5000+px causing the header gradient
           to fill the entire viewport. AB#20068.

           The :not() scoping is critical: once mmenu inits we must NOT force
           display:block, otherwise the off-canvas drawer stays visible on
           desktop after a mobile→desktop resize (mmenu's own responsive CSS
           handles drawer visibility per viewport). */
        nav#menu:not(.mm-menu):not(.mm-init){display:none}
        .main-site-header{min-height:80px}
        .mobile-homepage-body-cover{display:none}
        .layout-fluid #site,.layout-fixed #site{position:relative}
        /* Pin logo dimensions so the small/large bundles arriving late don't shift the header height */
        header .logo{width:145px}
        @media (min-width:992px){header .logo{width:217px}}
        header .logo a img{width:100%;height:auto;display:block}

                // flight by the time the user is filling the form.
                var opts = { once: true, capture: true, passive: true };
                document.addEventListener('focusin', function (e) {
                    if (e.target && e.target.closest && e.target.closest('form')) loadCaptcha();
